attempts.summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ 4.3.5 cluster (node1/node2/node3, CentOS Stream 10) using the official RabbitMQ Cloudsmith el9 repos. Created a dedicated CA and per-node server certs; rabbitmq.conf enforces listeners.tcp=none / TLS-only AMQP on 5671 with ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true, so only clients presenting a certificate issued by this CA are accepted (verified both positive and negative cases at the TLS layer and at the AMQP/pika protocol layer). Management HTTP API (15672) is bound to each node's own cluster IP (not 0.0.0.0-equivalent wildcard reachability) and firewalld restricts 15672/4369/25672 to the 10.100.195.0/24 cluster subnet only, while 5671 stays open for external AMQPS clients. guest user removed; a cluster_admin administrator account created. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id + healthy cluster/service state, issued systemd reboot (ack returned pre-disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified RabbitMQ active with full 3/3 running nodes and zero network partitions after each restart, only proceeding to the next node once the cluster was fully healthy.
